papers.title: Image-guided alignment of consecutive multi-modal tissue slides.
papers.abstract: We present COAST (consecutive multi-omics alignment of spatial tissues), a method to reliably physically align consecutive tissue sections to produce a unified multi-modal molecular dataset suitable for downstream applications. COAST relies exclusively on the images associated with spatial data, eliminating the need for common molecular features or prior annotations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of COAST using spatial transcriptomics slides from different technologies, tissues, and resolutions, in which it achieves performance comparable to established uni-modal alignment tools. Applying C
papers.summary: COAST is a new method that aligns consecutive tissue sections imaged by different spatial omics technologies using only tissue images, without needing shared molecular features or annotations. It achieves alignment accuracy comparable to existing uni-modal tools across various tissues and resolutions, enabling the creation of unified multi-modal molecular datasets.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing and machine learning to identify a prognostic signature based on tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), revealing potential therapeutic targets. The findings suggest that TDT-related genes can stratify patients by risk and may inform treatment strategies, offering a new avenue for personalized oncology.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This paper presents a systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing. By generating matched short-read and long-read datasets, the authors evaluate the performance of various computational tools for isoform detection and quantification, providing guidance for method selection in full-length transcriptomics studies.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a new probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets with mixed-order tensors (e.g., a drug-response tensor with a transcriptomics matrix), combining group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. It learns interpretable latent factors that align shared variation across data types, enabling better integration of complex experimental designs.

papers.title: Integrated Genomic and Proteomic Analysis Reveals T-B Lymphocyte Signatures in the MYCN Driven "Immune Desert" of Specific Neuroblastoma Subtypes.
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically dissect how MYCN amplification shapes the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) in high-risk neuroblastoma, elucidating key mechanisms underlying immune evasion.
papers.summary: This study integrates genomic and proteomic data to characterize how MYCN amplification creates an 'immune desert' tumor microenvironment in high-risk neuroblastoma, identifying specific T and B lymphocyte signatures associated with immune evasion. The findings reveal key mechanisms by which MYCN-driven tumors suppress immune responses, offering potential targets for immunotherapy in this aggressive pediatric cancer.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics characterisation of RSPO2+ nucleus pulposus cells reveals a WNT/FN1-CD44 degenerative axis and therapeutic targets in IVDD.
papers.abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a common cause of chronic low back pain, imposing a significant economic and physiological burden on individuals and society worldwide. Although dysregulation of the WNT/β-catenin pathway is considered an important factor contributing to the dysfunction of nucleus pulposus (NP) cells and degradation of the extracellular matrix, the mechanisms by which specific subgroups of NP cells are activated and the maintenance of excessive activation of specific pathways remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize RSPO2+ nucleus pulposus cells in intervertebral disc degeneration, revealing a WNT/FN1-CD44 degenerative axis. The findings identify potential therapeutic targets for IVDD by linking specific NP cell subgroups to WNT pathway dysregulation and extracellular matrix degradation.

papers.title: Unraveling the pathogenic mechanisms of osteoarthritis and obesity: An integration of GWAS, cellular specificity, and spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically elucidate the shared and specific genetic basis of osteoarthritis (OA) and obesity by integrating large-scale genome-wide association study (GWAS) summary statistics, cross-tissue quantitative trait loci (QTLs), and single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data.
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS, QTL, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data to identify shared and tissue-specific genetic mechanisms underlying osteoarthritis and obesity. It reveals cellular and spatial contexts where genetic risk converges, offering insights into common pathogenic pathways.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing uncovers an immunosuppressive program in PDAC mast cells: tumour-driven activation, proliferation, and association with Treg recruitment.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is characterized by a highly immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment (TME), which contributes to its resistance to immunotherapy. Although mast cells (MCs) have been implicated in PDAC progression, their functional heterogeneity and candidate signaling models of immune modulation remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize mast cells in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), revealing a tumour-driven immunosuppressive program involving activation and proliferation. The authors identify a link between these mast cells and regulatory T cell (Treg) recruitment, suggesting a mechanism by which mast cells contribute to the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment and immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: GRAIL-heart: A graph attention network for inferring ligand-receptor interactions in spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication through ligand-receptor (L-R) interactions orchestrates cardiac development, homeostasis, and disease progression, yet existing computational methods cannot infer directional signalling networks or distinguish causal from correlational interactions in spatial transcriptomics data. We present GRAIL-Heart, a graph-attention-based framework that integrates spatial tissue topology with multi-task learning to predict context-dependent L-R interactions, reconstruct gene expression, and infer causal signalling pathways. Validated on 42,654 cells across six cardiac regions from
papers.summary: GRAIL-heart is a new graph-attention-based method that infers directional ligand-receptor interactions from spatial transcriptomics data, integrating tissue topology and multi-task learning to distinguish causal from correlational signaling. Validated on cardiac tissue, it reconstructs gene expression and predicts context-dependent cell-cell communication.

papers.title: Supermeres containing Discoidin Domain Receptor 1 extracellular domain promote collagen alignment and immune exclusion in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) is an effective treatment for microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) colorectal cancers (CRCs) that are highly infiltrated by CD8+ T cells. Microsatellite stable (MSS) CRCs are unresponsive to ICB, at least in part, due to the paucity of intratumoral CD8+ T cells. We recently identified Discoidin Domain Receptor 1 (DDR1) as one of four genes associated with CD8+ T-cell exclusion in MSS CRC. There are conflicting reports about the presence and role of the cleaved ectodomain (cECD) of DDR1 in mouse models of breast and pancreatic cancer. To explore the role of t
papers.summary: This study identifies supermeres—extracellular vesicles carrying the cleaved ectodomain of Discoidin Domain Receptor 1 (DDR1)—as key mediators of immune exclusion in microsatellite stable colorectal cancer. These supermeres promote collagen alignment and reduce CD8+ T-cell infiltration, providing a mechanistic explanation for the poor response of MSS CRC to immune checkpoint blockade and suggesting potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: SemanticST: A Scalable Multi-Contextual Graph Learning Framework for Uncovering Spatial Niches and Robust Multi-Sample Integration in Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) analysis is often hindered by technical limitations and methodological biases that let dominant signals overshadow subtle but crucial biological patterns, such as rare cell types and fine-grained heterogeneity. This is especially true for high-complexity datasets from platforms like Xenium. We present SemanticST, a graph neural network (GNN) framework that addresses this challenge through a fundamentally different design. SemanticST is the first GNN method to implement mini-batch training, enabling scalable analysis of massive ST datasets (validated on Xenium). Cru
papers.summary: SemanticST is a scalable graph neural network framework for spatial transcriptomics that uses mini-batch training to handle massive datasets (e.g., Xenium) and integrates multi-sample data by uncovering subtle biological patterns like rare cell types and fine-grained spatial niches that dominant signals often obscure.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling identifies a fibroblast-like endothelial state and the MDK-NCL signaling axis in prostate cancer microenvironment remodeling.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer exhibits substantial microenvironmental heterogeneity, but endothelial plasticity and its clinical relevance remain insufficiently characterized. In this study, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomic data, and bulk transcriptomic cohorts to investigate endothelial heterogeneity in prostate cancer. Single-cell analysis identified a fibroblast-like endothelial (FLE) population characterized by the coexistence of endothelial and stromal transcriptional features. Endothelial subclustering further revealed a mesenchymal-like subset enriched in extracellular
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to characterize endothelial heterogeneity in prostate cancer, identifying a novel fibroblast-like endothelial (FLE) population with mixed endothelial and stromal features. The FLE state is linked to microenvironment remodeling and the MDK-NCL signaling axis, offering new insights into tumor-stroma interactions and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A skin-kidney neutrophil axis links ultraviolet exposure to renal angiogenesis and tissue remodeling in healthy and lupus kidneys.
papers.abstract: Neutrophils have been implicated in mediating immune crosstalk between injured tissue and distal organs, either promoting local and distal inflammation or mediating tissue repair. Skin injury from ultraviolet (UV) light triggers neutrophil migration to the kidney, which may have implications for nephritis flares in systemic lupus erythematosus. Here, we demonstrate that after skin exposure to UV light, renal neutrophils upregulate proangiogenic transcriptional programs and activate renal endothelial angiogenesis and tissue remodeling processes in healthy kidneys. Ligand-receptor analysis ident
papers.summary: This study reveals that ultraviolet (UV) skin exposure triggers a skin-kidney neutrophil axis, where neutrophils migrate to the kidney and adopt proangiogenic transcriptional programs, promoting renal angiogenesis and tissue remodeling. This mechanism operates in both healthy kidneys and may contribute to nephritis flares in lupus, highlighting a novel immune crosstalk pathway between skin and kidney.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analysis reveals 4-HNE-related stromal remodeling in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: 4-HNE is a lipid peroxidation product involved in oxidative stress, tumor microenvironment remodeling, and tumor progression. This study aimed to characterize the cellular distribution, prognostic relevance, and functional roles of 4-HNE-related molecular features in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular distribution and functional roles of 4-HNE, a lipid peroxidation product, in lung adenocarcinoma. The findings reveal that 4-HNE-related signaling is associated with stromal remodeling and has prognostic relevance, providing new insights into how oxidative stress shapes the tumor microenvironment.

papers.title: Benchmarking cell type annotation in spatial transcriptomics: resolving cellular hierarchies, biological fidelity, and dynamic cell states.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables the quantification of gene expression within its native tissue context, providing unprecedented insight into tissue architecture, cellular ecosystems, and local cell-cell interactions at regional and single-cell resolution. Accurate cell type annotation is a critical prerequisite for interpreting these data and is often the first and most essential step in downstream analysis. Despite rapid advances in computational methods, cell type annotation remains challenging and frequently requires extensive expert-driven manual curation based on marker-gene expression, s
papers.summary: This preprint benchmarks computational methods for cell type annotation in spatial transcriptomics, focusing on their ability to resolve cellular hierarchies, maintain biological fidelity, and capture dynamic cell states. The study provides a systematic evaluation that highlights current challenges and guides method selection for accurate annotation.

papers.title: Pan-tumor spatial transcriptomics reveals conserved properties of tumor organization.
papers.abstract: Tumor microenvironments (TMEs) are compositionally and functionally heterogeneous, making it challenging to discover organizing structural principles. Through a study of 262 solid tumors profiled by spatial transcriptomics, we identify a conserved architecture where TMEs are partitioned into discrete, hierarchically organized multicellular sub-regions, which we term "spatial groups" (SGs). As indicated by orthogonal spatial measurements and expert pathologist review, SGs associate with recognizable biological domains spanning global tissue context to local cellular neighborhoods. Comparing tum
papers.summary: This study analyzes spatial transcriptomics data from 262 solid tumors and identifies a conserved organizational architecture in the tumor microenvironment, where tissues are partitioned into discrete, hierarchically organized multicellular regions termed 'spatial groups' (SGs). These SGs correspond to recognizable biological domains, from global tissue context to local cellular neighborhoods, as validated by orthogonal spatial measurements and pathologist review. The findings reveal common structural principles underlying tumor organization across diverse cancer types.

papers.title: Lactylation-related immune-metabolic dysregulation defines prognostic and therapeutic stratification in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lactylation links lactate metabolism with inflammatory signaling and immune regulation in tumors. However, its cellular distribution and translational value in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain unclear.
papers.summary: This study investigates lactylation-related immune-metabolic dysregulation in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), revealing that lactylation patterns are associated with distinct immune and metabolic profiles that can stratify patients by prognosis and therapeutic response. The findings suggest that lactylation-related gene signatures could serve as biomarkers for personalized treatment strategies in LUAD.

papers.title: Maladaptive immune-fibrotic axis drives impaired long bone regeneration under mechanical instability.
papers.abstract: Delayed and nonhealing fractures, affecting 5 to 10% of cases, are associated with prolonged disability and diminished quality of life. Although acute inflammation is required to initiate repair, persistent mechanical instability can sustain maladaptive immune and fibrotic responses that impede regeneration. Existing animal models do not adequately recapitulate mechanical instability, the principal driver of hypertrophic nonunion in clinical settings, thereby limiting translational relevance. We developed a murine model of delayed fracture healing using tunable intramedullary fixation to impos
papers.summary: This study introduces a new mouse model of delayed fracture healing that mimics mechanical instability, a key driver of nonunion in patients. Using this model, the authors identify a maladaptive immune-fibrotic axis that impairs long bone regeneration under unstable conditions, offering a more translationally relevant platform for studying and treating nonhealing fractures.

papers.title: Current Advances in Spatial Pathology of Nasal Polyps: Challenges, Opportunities for Artificial Intelligence, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is characterized by inflammatory heterogeneity, epithelial hyperplasia, and tissue remodeling, with spatial pathology critical for deciphering pathological mechanisms and guiding clinical practice. Conventional histopathological techniques rely on subjective visual evaluation, limited by inadequate spatial resolution of molecular markers and imprecise quantitative analysis. Recent advances show that spatial transcriptomics reveals nasal polyps (NP) inflammatory heterogeneity; deep learning enables automated inflammatory subset identification an
papers.journal: World journal of otorhinolaryngology - head and neck surgery
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial pathology techniques, including spatial transcriptomics and deep learning-based image analysis, are advancing the understanding of chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP). It highlights the limitations of conventional histopathology and the potential of these new methods to reveal inflammatory heterogeneity and improve clinical practice.

papers.title: Spatially-resolved pharmaco-ecology of immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics for mechanism-matched combination therapies.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have reshaped the treatment landscape of lung adenocarcinoma, but primary, adaptive and acquired resistance are still the main clinical obstacles. This review integrates LUAD-specific evidence with broader NSCLC single-cell and spatial-omics studies, emphasizing lung adenocarcinoma where subtype-specific data are available. We discuss how therapeutic stress can select or induce malignant epithelial states that manifest as impaired antigen presentation, altered interferon signaling, partial epithelial-mesenchymal transition, stress tolerance, and hypoxia-related met
papers.summary: This review synthesizes single-cell and spatial transcriptomics evidence to explain how immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance arises in lung adenocarcinoma through therapy-induced malignant cell states, including impaired antigen presentation and altered interferon signaling. It proposes mechanism-matched combination therapies guided by spatially resolved pharmaco-ecology, offering a framework for overcoming immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: st2traj: deconvolution-informed trajectory inference for multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics enables study of developmental processes in native tissue context, but cell-state mixtures within spots and lack of direct spatial correspondence across sections complicate trajectory inference and biological interpretation.
papers.summary: This paper introduces st2traj, a computational method that integrates deconvolution with trajectory inference to analyze multi-timepoint spatial transcriptomics data. It addresses the challenges of cell-state mixtures within spatial spots and the lack of direct spatial correspondence across sections, enabling more accurate developmental trajectory reconstruction and biological interpretation.

papers.title: [Cellular barcoding and next-generation lineage tracing: concepts and applications].
papers.abstract: Lineage tracing is a fundamental technique for dissecting cell fate decisions and development process. With recent advances in high-throughput sequencing and single-cell sequencing technologies, cellular barcoding-based lineage tracing strategies have transitioned from low-throughput labeling methods to high-resolution, multidimensional lineage reconstruction. In this review, we systematically summarize four major barcoding paradigms: viral integration-based random integration barcodes, transposon-based random integration barcodes, recombinase-mediated DNA rearrangement (e.g., Cre-loxP), and C
papers.journal: Sheng li xue bao : [Acta physiologica Sinica]
papers.summary: This review systematically summarizes four major cellular barcoding paradigms for lineage tracing—viral integration, transposon integration, recombinase-mediated DNA rearrangement, and CRISPR-based editing—highlighting how advances in high-throughput and single-cell sequencing have enabled high-resolution, multidimensional lineage reconstruction. It provides a conceptual framework for selecting appropriate barcoding strategies in developmental biology and stem cell research.

papers.title: Hepatic and Brain Spatial Gene Expression Changes in Intragastric Alcohol Fed APP/PS1 Alzheimer's Disease Mouse Model.
papers.abstract: Background Alcohol use is increasingly recognized as a significant modifier of Alzheimer's disease (AD) risk and progression. Two key organs, the liver and the brain, are central to understanding the impact of alcohol intake on AD. This is due to the liver being the primary site of alcohol detoxification and a major target of alcohol-induced injury, while the brain harbors the neuropathological hallmarks of AD. Although growing literature now links liver dysfunction to AD pathogenesis, the molecular mechanisms linking peripheral alcohol-induced liver injury to brain pathology remain poorly def
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how alcohol consumption affects gene expression in the liver and brain of an Alzheimer's disease mouse model using spatial transcriptomics. It identifies coordinated molecular changes in both organs, suggesting that alcohol-induced liver injury may influence brain pathology through shared or communicating pathways. The study provides a resource for understanding the liver-brain axis in alcohol-exacerbated AD.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning to identify specific subsets of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and chronic inflammation signatures that are associated with poor outcomes in ovarian cancer, particularly after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The findings highlight these CAF subsets as potential drivers of residual disease and adverse prognosis, offering new targets for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Multimodal Analysis Reveals Aberrant Expression of SUMO2 and Its Significant Association With Key Mechanisms of Metabolic Pathways in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the third leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. However, the role of small ubiquitin-like modifier 2 (SUMO2), a core member of the small ubiquitin-like modifier (SUMO) family, regarding its expression patterns and metabolism-related functions in HCC remains inadequately understood.
papers.summary: This study investigates the expression and role of SUMO2 in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), finding that SUMO2 is aberrantly expressed and significantly associated with key metabolic pathways. The results suggest SUMO2 may play a role in HCC metabolism and could be a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: A categorization of spatial transcriptomics methods for cell-cell communication analysis.
papers.abstract: Cell-cell communication (CCC) is involved in regulating cellular behavior in tissues. Spatial transcriptomics adds local context to gene expression, enabling more biologically grounded CCC inference than single-cell RNA-seq alone. Rapid method development has yielded diverse CCC methods, each addressing distinct biological questions through varied analytical frameworks. We review 33 recent methods and organize them into three categories: inference of communication networks at cell-type or single-cell resolution, modeling of microenvironment-driven transcriptional variability and regulatory mod
papers.summary: This review categorizes 33 recent spatial transcriptomics methods for analyzing cell-cell communication (CCC) into three groups based on their analytical frameworks, helping researchers choose appropriate tools for their biological questions. It highlights how spatial context improves CCC inference compared to single-cell RNA-seq alone.

papers.title: A Neuro-Immune Score Defines a Stromal-Neural and Immune-Segregated Microenvironment Associated with Poor Prognosis in Colorectal Cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer progression and therapeutic response are determined not only by tumor-intrinsic programs but also by neural, stromal, and immune components of the tumor microenvironment. However, biologically interpretable transcriptomic scores that jointly capture neural/stromal remodeling and immune activation remain limited. We developed a neuro-immune score (NIS), defined as the neural/stromal module score minus the immune activation module score. NIS was constructed using the combined TCGA-COAD/READ colorectal cancer cohort and externally evaluated in independent Gene Expression Omnibus
papers.summary: The authors developed a neuro-immune score (NIS) that captures the balance between neural/stromal remodeling and immune activation in colorectal cancer. They found that a high NIS, indicating a stromal-neural enriched and immune-segregated microenvironment, is associated with poor prognosis, providing a biologically interpretable transcriptomic score for patient stratification.

papers.title: Single cell CRISPR screen identifies antagonism between Nsd1-H3K36me2 and Ezh2-H3K27me3 orchestrates pluripotency transition.
papers.abstract: The transcriptional and epigenetic landscape imposes constraints on the self-renewal capacity and lineage specification potential of both naive and primed mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs). CRISPR/Cas9-based functional screening coupled with single-cell RNA-seq (CROP-seq) establishes relationships between gRNA-mediated knockout genotype and transcriptome phenotype, providing a powerful tool to dissect gene regulatory networks. Here, we employed CROP-seq to investigate the epigenetic regulation governing the pluripotency network in mESCs. This highly sensitive method identified key genes essen
papers.summary: This study uses CROP-seq, a single-cell CRISPR screen, to identify epigenetic regulators essential for pluripotency transition in mouse embryonic stem cells. It reveals an antagonistic relationship between Nsd1-mediated H3K36me2 and Ezh2-mediated H3K27me3 that orchestrates the switch between naive and primed pluripotency states.

papers.title: Targeting breast cancer stem cells by restoring RBM38 function: mechanism and protein delivery therapy.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer stemness drives tumor progression and therapy resistance, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. In this study, we observed that RBM38 expression gradually decreases during breast cancer progression in MMTV-PyMT transgenic mice. Using a model with targeted RBM38 expression in breast tissue, we found it suppressed tumor initiation, decreased tumor size and metastasis, and reduced breast cancer stem cells. Multi-omics analyses, including single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, RIP-sequencing, and proteomics, were used to reveal the mechanisms. We identified HOXD10
papers.summary: This study identifies RBM38 as a tumor suppressor that is progressively lost during breast cancer progression, and restoring its expression suppresses tumor initiation, growth, and metastasis by reducing cancer stem cells. Using multi-omics approaches, the authors uncover a mechanism involving HOXD10 and demonstrate the potential of a protein delivery therapy to restore RBM38 function, offering a new therapeutic strategy for targeting breast cancer stemness.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Omics Technologies in Rice Abiotic Stress Biology: A Methodological Review.
papers.abstract: Abiotic stresses-drought, salinity, extreme temperature, flooding, and heavy-metal toxicity-constrain rice (Oryza sativa L.) yield worldwide, and the cellular programmes underlying them are unevenly distributed across cell types that bulk-tissue assays average together. This review examines, from a methodological standpoint, what single-cell and spatial omics technologies can and cannot establish about rice abiotic stress biology. We first define the modality space: single-cell omics measures RNA, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation, protein, or metabolite features at the resolution of in
papers.summary: This methodological review assesses the current and potential applications of single-cell and spatial omics technologies—such as transcriptomics, epigenomics, proteomics, and metabolomics—for studying rice responses to abiotic stresses like drought, salinity, and temperature extremes. It highlights how these approaches can resolve cell-type-specific stress programs that bulk assays obscure, while also discussing their technical limitations and challenges in rice.

papers.title: Spatial Immune Coding in Tumor-Draining Lymph Nodes: Functional Compartmentalization of Immune Activation and Immunosuppression.
papers.abstract: Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are important immune organs linking primary tumors with systemic immune responses. They support tumor antigen presentation, T-cell priming, and effector immune responses, but under sustained tumor influence they can also be remodeled into microenvironments that promote immune escape and metastatic colonization. Conventional methods, including flow cytometry, bulk RNA sequencing, and routine immunohistochemistry, have advanced our understanding of TDLN immunity but cannot simultaneously preserve tissue architecture, cell identity, and spatial cell-cell relatio
papers.summary: This review discusses how tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) can either support anti-tumor immunity or become immunosuppressive niches, and highlights the emerging role of spatial omics technologies in revealing the functional compartmentalization of immune activation and suppression within these tissues. The authors argue that spatial approaches can preserve tissue architecture and cell-cell interactions, offering a more complete understanding of TDLN biology than conventional methods.

papers.title: The gut-immune-brain axis in CNS tumors: Causal roles of microbiota and inflammatory proteins unveiled by Mendelian randomization and single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: There is a growing number of research suggesting that there is an association between gut microbiota and central nervous system (CNS) tumor. However, the causal relationships and the mediation effects of inflammatory proteins in the associations are unclear. We extracted genetic variants associated with gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and 4 subtypes of CNS tumors from published genome-wide association studies and performed a Mendelian randomization analysis to identify potential causal effects. The inverse variance weighted method was used as the main method. Mediation analysis and sing
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization to investigate causal links between gut microbiota, inflammatory proteins, and CNS tumors, finding potential causal effects and mediation pathways. Single-cell transcriptomics further supports the gut-immune-brain axis in tumor development.

papers.title: VIDEO-Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization: a tool for integrating and visualizing chromatin accessibility, in vivo transcription factor binding and motif occurrence in tissue-specific differentially expressed genes.
papers.abstract: Dissecting gene regulation today relies on many genomic assays-including transcriptional output from RNA-seq, chromatin accessibility from ATAC-seq, and transcription factor (TF) binding from ChIP-seq. Whereas numerous tools exist for each modality and some integrate data across modalities, few allow researchers to interactively explore and visualize how TF binding motifs intersect with transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility in a tissue-specific context. Here we introduce VIDEO (Visual Integration of Drosophila Enhancer Organization), a web-based analysis tool that enables visual
papers.summary: VIDEO is a new web-based tool that integrates and visualizes chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, and motif occurrence data in a tissue-specific context for Drosophila. It allows researchers to interactively explore how TF binding motifs intersect with transcriptional activity and chromatin accessibility, addressing a gap in existing genomic analysis tools.

papers.title: ScanNet: Single-cell annotation informed by transcriptional regulation Network via iterative heterogeneous graph learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate annotation of cell types in single-cell transcriptome sequencing (scRNA-seq) data is critical for understanding cellular identities. The transcriptional regulatory networks (TRNs), which map the regulatory relationships between transcription factors (TFs) and their target genes (TGs), capture the molecular dependencies underlying transcriptional programs. However, most existing cell type annotation methods do not fully exploit this regulatory information. Therefore, we introduce ScanNet, a Single cell annotation method informed by transcriptional regulation Network, to integrate prior
papers.summary: ScanNet is a new computational method that improves cell type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing data by integrating transcriptional regulatory network information through iterative heterogeneous graph learning. It outperforms existing methods by leveraging regulatory relationships between transcription factors and target genes, providing more accurate cell type identification.

papers.title: Benchmarking computational decontamination of ambient RNA.
papers.abstract: Gene expression profiling of single cells using single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (sxRNA-seq) enables researchers to characterize cellular heterogeneity and unraveling complex biological processes at unprecedented resolution. However, sxRNA-seq faces challenges due to the presence of ambient RNA, extraneous RNA molecules not originating from the cells of interest. Sample preparation is a major source of ambient RNA, where harsh conditions can lead to cell lysis and the release of intracellular RNA. This inescapable inclusion of ambient RNA can cause erroneous results and hinder dow
papers.summary: This paper benchmarks computational methods for removing ambient RNA contamination from single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data. It evaluates the performance of existing decontamination tools, likely using simulated or real datasets, to guide researchers in choosing appropriate methods. The findings provide practical recommendations for improving data quality in single-cell transcriptomics studies.

papers.title: Multi-omics identification of MBNL2 associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (NACI) improves outcomes in resectable lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), yet response varies widely and current biomarkers lack precision. Novel correlates of immunotherapy sensitivity tailored to the LUSC tumor microenvironment (TME) are urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics analysis to identify MBNL2 as a potential biomarker associated with poor pathological response to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy in lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC). The findings suggest that MBNL2 expression in the tumor microenvironment may help predict which patients are less likely to benefit from this treatment, addressing the need for more precise biomarkers in LUSC.

papers.title: Bulk and single cell RNA sequencing data reveal lactylation-related gene signatures for prognosis and immunity in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: Previous studies indicate that lactylation, a post-translational modification, may play an important role in the progression of cervical cancer (CC). However, the comprehensive roles of lactylation in influencing the tumor microenvironment, immune landscape, and prognosis of CC have yet to be fully elucidated. The bulk RNA-seq and single-cell RNA-seq datasets of CC patients were downloaded from the Cancer Genome Atlas and Gene Expression Omnibus databases, respectively. A total of 630 genes associated with lactylation activity were identified using AUCell algorithm, differential expression, an
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study analyzed bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing data from cervical cancer patients to identify lactylation-related gene signatures. The authors found that these signatures are associated with prognosis and the immune landscape, suggesting lactylation plays a role in tumor progression and immunity in cervical cancer.

papers.title: EMCN is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and represents a potential biomarker in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: While MUC family genes have been established as prognostic biomarkers in gastric cancer, and GWAS studies link EMCN mutations to chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in NSCLC, the systematic characterization of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains elusive.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of EMCN in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), finding that EMCN expression is associated with vascular-immune crosstalk and may serve as a potential prognostic biomarker. The authors provide a systematic characterization of EMCN in LUAD, which had been previously underexplored.

papers.title: Prognostic significance of ZNF695 in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma: single-cell and immune infiltration analyses.
papers.abstract: Zinc Finger Protein 695 (ZNF695) has been reported as a prognostic indicator in several cancers; however, its clinical implications and functional contributions within uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) have not yet been elucidated. Herein, the prognostic significance of ZNF695 in UCEC and its potential involvement in immune infiltration were examined.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of ZNF695 in uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC), finding that its expression is associated with patient prognosis and immune cell infiltration. Using single-cell and immune infiltration analyses, the authors suggest ZNF695 could serve as a prognostic biomarker in UCEC.

papers.title: IL1RAP Is Associated With an Inflammation-Immunity-Related State in Skin Cutaneous Melanoma: Integrative Evidence From Pan-Cancer Data and Melanoma Immunotherapy Cohorts.
papers.abstract: The crosstalk between inflammation and immunity plays a central role in tumor progression, immune evasion, and therapeutic response. Interleukin-1 receptor accessory protein (IL1RAP) is a key adaptor in inflammatory signaling, yet its immunological relevance and clinical implications in skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) remain largely unexplored.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of IL1RAP in skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM) using pan-cancer data and melanoma immunotherapy cohorts. The authors find that IL1RAP is associated with an inflammation-immunity-related state, suggesting it may serve as a biomarker or therapeutic target in SKCM.

papers.title: Inhibition of Cyclin-dependent Kinase Counteracts Neuron-promoted Bladder and Endometrial Tumorigenesis: A Systematic Analysis.
papers.abstract: The tumor microenvironment is an indispensable component of tumor development. Although fibroblasts and immune cells have been widely studied in tumorigenesis, the role of neurons in cancer has received limited investigation. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of neural signaling on tumorigenesis across cancer types and identify potential therapeutics for neuron-associated tumor development.
papers.summary: This study systematically investigates how neural signaling in the tumor microenvironment influences bladder and endometrial tumorigenesis, finding that inhibiting cyclin-dependent kinase counteracts neuron-promoted tumor growth. The results suggest CDK inhibitors as potential therapeutics for neuron-associated cancers.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial landscape reveals impaired tertiary lymphoid structure maturation in Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric cancer.
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) are key immune niches involved in antitumor immunity. However, their functional impact depends on spatial localization, maturation status, and cellular composition within the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). Despite the recognized role of Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) in gastric carcinogenesis and immune modulation, its influence on TLS architecture and function in gastric cancer remains poorly understood.
papers.summary: This study maps tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in Helicobacter pylori-associated gastric cancer using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics, revealing that TLS maturation is impaired in these tumors. The findings suggest that H. pylori infection disrupts TLS architecture and function, potentially contributing to immune evasion in gastric cancer.

papers.title: FN1-associated cavernous endothelial remodeling induced by bisphenol A: relevance to erectile dysfunction and attenuation by baicalin.
papers.abstract: Previous studies suggest that bisphenol A (BPA) exposure may impair erectile function, but the underlying cavernous endothelial mechanisms remain unclear. Whether BPA induces endothelial alterations resembling those in diabetic erectile dysfunction (DMED) is unknown.
papers.summary: This study investigates how bisphenol A (BPA) exposure impairs erectile function by remodeling cavernous endothelial cells, potentially through FN1-associated pathways, and whether these changes mimic diabetic erectile dysfunction. The authors also explore the protective effects of baicalin, a natural compound, in attenuating BPA-induced endothelial damage.

papers.title: Disease-specific biomarker value of C-reactive protein and its composite indices in autoinflammatory diseases: an integrated study of multi-modal omics and population cohorts.
papers.abstract: Autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs) are a heterogeneous group of innate immune-driven disorders whose prevalence is rising globally, yet the lack of disease-specific biomarkers continues to hamper accurate disease activity assessment, phenotype stratification, and risk evaluation. C-reactive protein (CRP) is one of the most widely used markers of systemic inflammation, yet its disease-specific expression, clinical correlations, network connectivity, and cellular origin across both adult and pediatric AIDs have not been systematically examined.
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates C-reactive protein (CRP) and its composite indices as disease-specific biomarkers across multiple autoinflammatory diseases (AIDs), integrating multi-modal omics data and population cohorts. The findings reveal disease-specific CRP expression patterns, clinical correlations, and cellular origins, potentially improving disease activity assessment and phenotype stratification in both adult and pediatric AIDs.
